The content-root-consumer residue class has a production fix now, in the SOURCE repo, commit 285a7a957. Root cause, one sentence: the split gave MSBuild the workspace roots and the running program none. The contract already existed and was correct (tools/seedsmith/seedsmith/workspace_roots.py, which even names its twin and says 'a root is never guessed'); what was missing is that tests/Shared/KeepverseRoots.cs was the ONLY C# implementation and it is linked into *.Tests alone. ADDED src/FusionRpg.Core/Workspace/KeepverseRoots.cs (net6.0, Unity-free, no SQL; guard-dal and guard-secondary-no-unity both OK), mirroring the Python contract exactly. SeedImportRunner.FindUp gains a pre-pass and KEEPS its walk, because a monorepo checkout must return byte-identical answers and dist/FusionRpg.Server/data (a real call site in AtomImporter and CreatureSpeciesImport) is in neither root. The file blob at dbba30c and at HEAD is identical (686224b9d300), so the content I described in that message - a seven-section document with a four-row refusal table and a scripts section - is not what that commit contains. Its own description of correcting section 4 was also overtaken: 888fd44 rewrote that section again after me. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the third time in this migration that a provenance claim was asserted without the command that settles it, and the first time it was in MY OWN commit message rather than in a report. The earlier two were a count that excluded copies and an A7 scan whose needles matched code paths. The pattern is the claim; the surface varies. I also wrote a PowerShell ancestry test that reported b4d359e and dbba30c as unrelated because 'if (git merge-base --is-ancestor ...)' tests the command's OUTPUT, which is empty, not its exit code - so it printed 'no' for a pair that is in fact linearly ordered. A broken test that returns a confident wrong answer is worse than no test. NOT AMENDED, per the no-amend rule. Corrected here and in the follow-up commit instead. LANE 3's own work stands on its merits and was reviewed, not discarded: its seal design is sound, its 14 tests all fail against the pre-change tool, its section 8 independently measured the same 132-file scripts figure I measured, and it had already recorded the finding with an owner and a reason. The commit added on top of it adds the evidence that changes the reason from 'deferred pending a judgement about 132 files' to 'the obvious move breaks gk-core's build and its standalone clone', with the four-part change set that has to happen instead - including that two of the six consumers are .ps1 files the ps1-ban program is already retiring and must not be given a new home. LANE RESTART RULE, restated because it is now measured rather than assumed: a lane that dies on a transport error may have already committed. Before restarting a lane, read git log for its fence and check whether its work is already at HEAD. Restarting blind risks a second lane redoing or contradicting the first.

So the majority marker is a cross-repository reference created by the split. THE COMPOUNDING DEFECT, which matters more than the marker: roughly 37 of those files carry a [ModuleInitializer]. A module initializer that throws runs at ASSEMBLY LOAD, so one unresolvable path fails EVERY test in the assembly - observed directly: FusionRpg.Core.Workspace.Tests failed 9 of 9 with System.TypeInitializationException from '<Module>' before a single test body ran, and FusionRpg.E2E.Tests failed 296 of 296 the same way. A TESTED C# LEXER, because the root cause of both earlier transform failures is now named. Neither the naive brace counter nor a first-draft tokenizer handles an interpolation hole that CONTAINS A NESTED STRING LITERAL. The real cases in this repo are src/FusionRpg.Data/Sqlite/LegacyMonoMigrator.cs:197 $"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS \"{table.Replace(" ... , an interpolated string whose hole opens a nested string. A lexer that ends the literal at the hole's first inner quote leaves a real '{' outside the string, and every brace count after that point is wrong - which is the 30 CS1519 'Invalid token throw in a member declaration' from the previous row, and it is a lexer bug, not a C# syntax problem. The lexer now tokenizes comments (nested block comments included), char literals, regular, verbatim and raw string literals, and every interpolation form, and scans an interpolation hole as CODE - a hole may contain a nested literal, and that literal's quotes must not be mistaken for the enclosing literal's closer. A '{' is a hole only in a $-prefixed literal; in a plain string it is an ordinary character, and treating it as a hole made an early draft swallow real code (1782 files wrongly reported unbalanced, versus 28 now). PROOF IT BITES, because an untested parser is the thing being replaced: 14 adversarial shapes are asserted, including hole-with-nested-string, hole-with-escaped-quote, raw-interpolated-hole, verbatim-doubled-quotes, char-literal-brace and nested block comment. Two structural properties are asserted over all 3522 .cs files: mask() preserves length exactly on 400 files, and match_brace produces a proper nesting (equal open/close counts, every '{' pairs forward, intervals never cross) on a real file. 28 real files remain unprovable, mostly raw interpolated strings and one double-dollar raw string - that residual is the reason for the refusal below rather than a reason to trust the tool more.
